title: PRD update: Customer SLA notifications and automated remediation playbooks for incident-driven degradations
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD update codifies a new product requirement: automatically translate postmortem action items and SLO breaches into customer-facing SLA notifications and automated remediation playbooks. The goal is to reduce time-to-remediation for tenant-impacting incidents and provide transparent, auditable communications to affected customers. This update scopes the product work (console surface, notification wiring, acceptance tests, and runbook automation) and clarifies trade-offs and constraints for engineering and support teams.

Context and motivation:
- Recent incidents highlighted delays between runtime detection, operator action, and customer communication. Postmortem actions recommend faster, standardized notifications plus automated remediation where safe.
- Customers demand clear SLA status, remediation timelines, and predictable fallback behaviors (especially Dedicated tenants).
- This feature ties three layers: detection (SLO engine), product surface (console + status + automated email/ops alerts), and remediation (playbook runner integrated with runtime).

Scope (what this ticket requires):
1) Console: per-tenant SLA status panel showing active degradations, expected remediation steps (human + automated), and a history of notifications.
2) Notification pipeline: automated generation of customer-facing messages when a scoped SLO breach or failure contract is triggered; messages include impact summary, estimated mitigation ETA, and link to remediation runbook.
3) Runbook automation: authorable playbooks (yaml) that can be executed by ops tooling; safe hypothesis: some remediation steps are allowed to be executed automatically (e.g., traffic re-routing to healthy model variant) behind a feature flag and with rollback guardrails.
4) Acceptance tests: synthetic canaries and CI checks that validate notification generation, runbook execution (dry-run in staging), and console display before rollout.
5) Integrations: tie into Support ticketing (create/annotate tickets), Status Page (public incident window), and customer email webhook.

Out of scope for initial iteration:
- Full tenant billing adjustments tied to degradations (future work).
- Deep ML model retraining or model quality regression automation.

Design / UX notes:
- Console panel must provide concise timeline, remediation actions with author (human/automation), and a single "acknowledge" button for customer success to annotate communication.
- Notifications must be templated with variables (tenant, route, severity, ETA, mitigation steps) and stored in an auditable log.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Automated remediation vs. operator control: default is operator approval for high-impact tenants; allow opt-in automated remediation for low-risk mitigation (traffic routing, cache priming).
- Notification verbosity: favor concise summaries with link to detailed runbook to avoid noise.
- Scope of runbook actions allowed automatically will be limited and require a security review.

Links to artifacts:
- PRD doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/prd/sla-notifications-remediation
- UX mocks (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcdef/console-sla-panel
- Proposed runbook schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbook-schemas/pull/12
- Incident reference: https://internal.redwood.ai/postmortems/2025-01-kv-cache-stall

Owner notes for engineering:
- SLO detection events will include a new metadata field "customer_notification_level" to drive routing.
- Create an internal API endpoint (POST /internal/notifications) that accepts templated payloads and writes to notification log + external channels.
- Runbook runner must support dry-run mode (staging) and a gated autopilot flag for production.
acceptance_criteria: When a modeled SLO breach with customer impact is detected, an entry appears in the tenant's SLA panel in the Console within 2 minutes.
Automated customer notification (templated) is created and stored in the Notification Log; for P1 breaches the system opens or annotates a Support ticket with the notification payload.
Runbook designs exist in repo and a stage run triggers a dry-run execution with synthetic traffic; logs show steps and timing.
Console shows remediation status and allows operator acknowledgement; acknowledgement history is persisted and exportable as CSV.
Feature flag gating: autopilot runbook actions are disabled by default for tenants flagged as 'high-risk'; enabling requires operator confirmation and audit trail.
CI pipeline includes an e2e check that injects synthetic SLO breach and verifies notification pipeline, console display, and runbook dry-run in staging.
Security review completed for automated remediation actions and secrets access (KMS/HSM) if required.
